hero.title: Virtual Fiduciary File
hero.subtitle: Organize every fiduciary decision, benchmark, and committee record in one secure, well-organized location.

blocks.text: Good fiduciary decisions deserve good documentation.

ERISA requires retirement plan fiduciaries to demonstrate a prudent process—not simply make prudent decisions. If your committee cannot show when providers were benchmarked, investments were reviewed, or decisions were documented, it becomes difficult to demonstrate that your fiduciary responsibilities have been fulfilled.

PointOak's Virtual Fiduciary File keeps every important retirement plan document organized in one secure location. Committee minutes, investment reviews, fee benchmarking reports, governance records, provider evaluations, and fiduciary documentation are maintained throughout the year, giving your organization a complete record of its fiduciary process.

sections.title: Benefits of the Virtual Fiduciary File

body.text: A documented fiduciary process demonstrates that your committee consistently reviews investments, providers, fees, and governance responsibilities rather than relying on memory or scattered records.
Whether responding to a Department of Labor inquiry, onboarding a new committee member, or preparing for an internal review, every important document is organized and easily accessible.

Committee membership changes over time. Maintaining a complete fiduciary record allows new members to understand prior decisions, benchmark history, and ongoing responsibilities without recreating past work.
Keeping meeting minutes, investment reports, provider evaluations, and committee decisions together creates a repeatable governance process that supports consistent fiduciary oversight.

Instead of searching through emails, shared drives, and multiple vendors, your retirement plan documentation remains organized in one centralized location maintained as part of your ongoing consulting relationship.

sections.title: How the Virtual Fiduciary File Works

blocks.text: Every retirement plan produces documentation throughout the year. Investment reviews, provider benchmarking, committee meetings, fee analyses, governance updates, and compliance activities all contribute to your fiduciary record.

PointOak organizes those materials into a structured Virtual Fiduciary File that grows alongside your retirement plan. Rather than treating documentation as an annual project, we maintain it continuously as part of your ongoing fiduciary process.
The result is a complete, well-organized record that supports committee decision-making, regulatory readiness, and long-term governance.

items.q: What is a Virtual Fiduciary File?

a.text: A Virtual Fiduciary File is a secure, organized repository that stores the documents supporting your retirement plan's fiduciary process.

Rather than keeping committee minutes, investment reports, fee benchmarks, provider evaluations, and governance documents in multiple locations, everything is maintained in one centralized location. The result is a complete fiduciary record that supports committee continuity, regulatory readiness, and ongoing governance.

items.q: What documents should be included in a retirement plan fiduciary file?

a.text: A comprehensive fiduciary file should include committee meeting minutes, investment reviews, fee benchmarking reports, provider evaluations, governance documents, Investment Policy Statements, fiduciary policies, and documentation supporting major committee decisions.
The goal is to demonstrate a consistent, well-documented fiduciary process over time rather than isolated decisions.

items.q: Does ERISA require a fiduciary file?

a.text: ERISA requires fiduciaries to act prudently and document their decision-making process, but it does not prescribe one specific filing system.

Maintaining an organized fiduciary file is considered a best practice because it allows committees to demonstrate ongoing oversight, provider monitoring, investment review, and governance activities if questions arise.

items.q: How often should fiduciary documentation be updated?

a.text: Documentation should be updated whenever significant fiduciary activities occur.

Committee meetings, quarterly investment reviews, benchmarking studies, provider evaluations, governance updates, and major plan decisions should all be incorporated into the fiduciary record as they happen rather than collected at year-end.

items.q: What happens if the Department of Labor audits our retirement plan?

a.text: A well-organized fiduciary file allows your organization to quickly locate documentation supporting provider selection, fee benchmarking, investment monitoring, committee decisions, and governance practices.
Having organized documentation can significantly simplify the audit process and demonstrate a prudent fiduciary approach.

items.q: Who should have access to the Virtual Fiduciary File?

a.text: Access is typically limited to individuals with fiduciary responsibilities, such as retirement plan committee members, HR leadership, finance executives, legal counsel, and authorized advisors.
Maintaining controlled access helps protect sensitive plan information while ensuring the committee can retrieve documentation when needed.

items.q: Can PointOak maintain our fiduciary documentation for us?

a.text: Maintaining your Virtual Fiduciary File is part of PointOak's broader fiduciary consulting approach. As we perform investment reviews, benchmarking, governance support, and committee consulting, the related documentation is organized and maintained throughout the engagement.

items.q: Does the Virtual Fiduciary File replace our recordkeeper's documents?

a.text: Your recordkeeper maintains participant records and plan administration documents. The Virtual Fiduciary File complements those records by organizing the committee's governance documentation, fiduciary analyses, benchmarking reports, investment reviews, and decision-making records that typically are not maintained by the recordkeeper.
